Its extreme salinity is due to a combination of geological and chemical factors. Geologically, the Dead Sea lies in a rift valley formed by the movement of the African and Arabian tectonic plates, creating a deep basin with no natural outflow, safe. Chemically, the region experiences high evaporation rates due to its hot, arid climate, which leaves behind dissolved minerals and salts, safe.
